job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

passage: Many people mistakenly believe that poverty is simply a result of personal laziness or a lack of hard work. In reality, poverty is a complex issue rooted in historical exploitation, lack of land resources, and limited access to quality education or healthcare. Because circumstances vary across different regions, the poverty line is not a single fixed amount for every individual; instead, it is calculated based on minimum subsistence levels of food, clothing, and shelter, which differ between rural and urban areas. To combat these systemic challenges, the government implements various social welfare programs. One such initiative is the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). It is important to understand that MGNREGA does not provide permanent, lifelong employment to every citizen. Rather, it acts as a crucial safety net by guaranteeing at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to rural households whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. By providing this temporary income support, the scheme helps vulnerable families survive during lean agricultural seasons and prevents them from falling deeper into destitution. Poverty is a structural problem that requires government intervention and social support, not just individual effort.

items.evidence: In reality, poverty is a complex issue rooted in historical exploitation, lack of land resources, and limited access to quality education or healthcare.
items.q: Meena works hard daily but owns no land and cannot reach a school. Why might she stay poor?
options: Lack of resources and services keeps her poor
Lack of effort in her daily work keeps her poor
Lack of space from rising population keeps her poor
Lack of a move to the city keeps her poor
items.explain: Poverty comes from lack of land, education and healthcare, not from laziness.

wrong.why: thinks poor people do not work hard enough
thinks population growth is the only cause
thinks cities have no poor people

items.evidence: Because circumstances vary across different regions, the poverty line is not a single fixed amount for every individual; instead, it is calculated based on minimum subsistence levels of food, clothing, and shelter, which differ between rural and urban areas.
items.q: A student says one poverty line fits everyone in India. Why is this wrong?
options: Basic needs differ between villages and cities
Each family sets the line by its own wishes
Only villages have poor people to measure
Hard workers are given a lower line
items.explain: The line depends on minimum food, clothing and shelter needs, which differ in rural and urban areas.

wrong.why: thinks families set the line themselves
thinks poverty exists only in villages
links poverty to how hard people work

items.evidence: Rather, it acts as a crucial safety net by guaranteeing at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to rural households whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
items.q: Ramu's village household signs up for MGNREGA. What can they expect from it?
options: At least 100 days of paid work a year
A lifelong job for every adult member
Paid office work at a city company
Free money each month without any work
items.explain: MGNREGA guarantees at least 100 days of wage work yearly to rural households, not lifelong jobs.

wrong.why: ignores that it is rural and manual work
mixes up wage employment with free handouts

items.evidence: By providing this temporary income support, the scheme helps vulnerable families survive during lean agricultural seasons and prevents them from falling deeper into destitution.
items.q: Why is MGNREGA most useful to rural families in the lean months between harvests?
options: It gives them earnings when other work is scarce
It makes them rich enough to stop farming
It teaches them to work harder than before
It moves them to cities where nobody is poor
items.explain: Its temporary income helps families survive lean farm seasons and stops them sinking deeper into poverty.

wrong.why: over-generalises temporary support into lasting wealth
thinks poverty is due to laziness
thinks cities have no poor people
